processing: Typical of Darjeeling: orthodox black tea, withered, rolled, oxidised and dried; lots are often sold under FTGFOP grades.
harvest_season: First flush in spring is the lot most often seen; other flushes follow the usual Darjeeling calendar.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf in mixed olive and brown, as usual for the region.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in first flush, deeper amber in later flushes.
taste_profile: Little is recorded for this garden alone. Expect the general Darjeeling pattern: floral and brisk in spring, fruitier and fuller in summer.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style, as for other Darjeeling. Use cooler water and a shorter steep for first flush.

vintage_note: Sold by flush and grade, First Flush FTGFOP being a common listing. As usual for Darjeeling, the year should be on the label; buy the latest harvest.
description:
Gielle is a Teesta Valley garden in Darjeeling, and one of the older names in the district according to the merchants who sell it. Its name is said to be linked to a local river.

The tea is made in the orthodox way, and merchants mention original China bushes. No independent account confirms the details of the planting.

In the cup, expect what is typical of Darjeeling: floral and brisk in spring, rounder later in the year. Brew it as you would any first flush, with water a little off the boil.

It turns up as a named lot at a number of European merchants, usually with a grade like FTGFOP. Grade letters describe the leaf more than the flavour, so check the year and flush too.
history:
Sellers date the estate to the early 1850s. These are merchant accounts, and no independent record has been traced. One seller gives an altitude of about 1,600 metres.

The gloss of the name as land of sweet water, said to be Lepcha, also comes from sellers, so take it lightly.
